answer: Picture each agent as a pigment on a shared palette: a sybil farm mixes one host into many shades, so everything comes out the same muddy violet. To catch that, the network asks random verifiers to ping an agent from several regions at unpredictable moments and triangulate its round-trip latency. Twenty "distinct" agents answering from one rack share the same timing signature and get merged into a single identity, while a lone saffron-bright operator keeps its own weight.
